cut_items.item: Distinguish leak vs. limit too low: if heap rises and falls but peaks near the limit, raise the limit rather than hunt a leak
In containers, keep --max-old-space-size below the container memory limit or the OS OOM-kills the process
Use --heapsnapshot-near-heap-limit=3 to capture a snapshot just before the crash in production
Warning not to expose node --inspect on a public port; option to attach DevTools to live process
Additional causes: unbounded queues/streams without backpressure; per-request data on long-lived objects / high-cardinality metrics labels
Use an LRU cache with a max size as the fix for unbounded caches
MaxListenersExceededWarning as a signal for listener leaks
Asks for Node version and container usage
Distinguishes a leak from a heap limit that is simply too low, by checking whether the heap rises and falls but peaks near the limit
In a container, keep --max-old-space-size below the container memory limit, or the OS OOM-kills the process
--heapsnapshot-near-heap-limit=3 writes a snapshot just before the crash, giving production evidence
Connect DevTools to the live process with node --inspect, and do not expose it on a public port
Use an LRU cache with a maximum size and expiry as the fix for unbounded caches
MaxListenersExceededWarning is the signal for listener leaks
Unbounded queues, or streams without backpressure when the producer outpaces the consumer, as a cause
Per-request data attached to long-lived objects, such as high-cardinality metrics labels or DB connections, as a cause
Asks whether the service runs in a container as a diagnostic question

added_items.item: Warning: heap snapshots pause the process and can use as much memory as the heap, so take them on one instance only in production to avoid triggering the crash
Use the Retainers view to see what holds the growing objects
Take a third snapshot later and look for types that grow in every snapshot
Final step: fix, redeploy and re-watch the memory trend to verify
Explains what a leak/GC is and notes a restart on memory threshold in the process manager
Unclosed streams, sockets, or database connections as a cause
Offers to help read snapshot output
Take three snapshots (early, later, even later) so growth can be seen across several, not just two
Open the Retainers view to see what holds the growing objects
Fix the code, redeploy, and watch the trend again to verify
